column11: Berakhot 54a: ‘The mishna articulates a general principle: One is obligated to recite a blessing for the bad that befalls him just as he recites a blessing for the good that befalls him, as it is stated: “And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might” (Deuteronomy 6:5). Alternatively, it may…’ Context and connection to Likkutei Maamarim: In Likkutei Maamarim, On Shimshon, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Berakhot 54a) to illuminate his argument here (“which is termed: 'with all your soul'—even if He takes your soul (ibid. 54a), which is death and the total shattering of the physical vessel; even so he completely nullifies his entire being before the Surrounding...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source grounds the spiritual dynamic of Torah, Israel's sanctity, and divine service developed in this discourse of Likkutei Maamarim.

column11: Shabbat 55b: ‘The Gemara now clarifies the matter: Who is the tanna of the baraita that states that four people did not die due to their own sins?
